title: Shantanu's promise
hookLine: a woman rises from the river and sits on a praying king's right thigh; years later his son gives her his word
tomorrow: what will Shantanu's promise cost him?
last: KARMA CARRIES INTO THE NEXT BIRTH.

lines: A WOMAN RISES FROM THE RIVER.
SHE SITS ON THE RIGHT THIGH.
cards: A king is sitting by the river, deep in prayer. His name is Pratipa. Out of the water rises a woman of great beauty, and she sits down on his right thigh.
Pratipa doesn't send her away, and he doesn't take her as a lover. Instead he tells her: the right thigh is for children and daughters-in-law. The left is for a wife.
You sat on the right, so you'll be my son's wife.

teach.b: The woman is Ganga, and she agrees: she'll marry Pratipa's son, on one condition, that whatever she does, he won't question it. A son is born: Shantanu, who is Mahabhisha come down from heaven.
When Shantanu is grown, Pratipa hands him the kingdom, and a message with it. A lovely woman may come to you. If she does, take her as your wife.
Don't ask who she is, and don't question what she does. One day, walking along the bank of the Ganga, Shantanu sees a woman by the water, and he's struck. He asks her to be his wife.
Whatever I do, good or bad, you must never stop me or speak harshly to me. The moment you do, I'll leave. He agrees.
Now notice what we know that he doesn't: she's Ganga, and she's promised the Vasus. He knows only that he's in love, and that he's given his word.

teach.h: A WORD IS NEVER SMALL TALK.
teach.b: In this epic, a given word is never small talk.
Keeping it is dharma, and the Mahabharata tests that again and again; one vow coming soon will shape the whole Kuru line. Hindus still make their biggest promises out loud and witnessed.
At a wedding, the couple circles the sacred fire and takes seven steps together, the saptapadi, with Agni, the fire, as witness.

Shantanu's vow had no fire and no family, only a riverbank and a man in love, and it will hold his tongue for years. They marry, and the text says they're happy together. And their first child is on the way.

how: At a Hindu wedding the couple walks around the sacred fire and takes seven steps together, the saptapadi, making their promises with Agni, the fire, as witness.

games.q: a friend wants you to promise to back them in a fight before telling you what it's about. by Shantanu's story, what fits?
o: ask first; a given word binds, so know what it asks.
promise now; you can always take it back later.
promise; a word given between friends doesn't really count.
games.why: Shantanu agreed before he knew who she was or what she'd do, and his word held him for years. in the epic, keeping your word is dharma; that's why it's worth asking first.

practice: Write down, by hand, one promise you're carrying right now: to a person, a team, yourself. If you can, light a candle or a small lamp beside it, the way a Hindu wedding keeps the fire as witness. Read the promise once, out loud.
Then ask, gently: do I still know what this promise asks of me?

wordCard.voice: Pratipa. The king who, when Ganga sat on his right thigh, told her she'd be his son's wife, and whose warning led Shantanu to vow never to question her.

orig.note: Sanskrit Śantanu, the Kuru king, son of Pratipa; in this story, Mahabhisha reborn.
